newsitem.title: UK: IATA sees five yr int'l passenger growth at 7.1pct.
newsitem.headline: IATA sees five yr int'l passenger growth at 7.1pct.

text.p: World international scheduled passenger traffic is now expected to grow at 7.1 percent a year between 1996-2000, compared to an earlier forecast of 6.6 percent , International Air Transport Association (IATA) economist Francois Dormoy said.
This is because growth in the large travel markets of Europe and North America "is not falling as much as might be expected" he told IATA's 10th Air Transport Outlook Conference.
Both are expected to experience growth at levels of six percent annually during the period, he said.
Another factor was continuing strong growth in Asian markets -- notable in China and Vietnam -- as well as Latin America and eastern Europe, he said

The 7.1 percent average for the period means world scheduled international passengers will jump to some 522 million passengers by the year 2000 from the present 371 million, a rise of 151 million passengers, he added.
IATA also expects growth at similar rates in the longer term and "somewhat higher than the five percent average IATA and other organisations frequently predicted in the past".
Dormoy said the average annual increase for the period 2001-2010 will be six percent, which will more than double the current passenger total to nearly 800 million.
But that is only 15 years away which "does not leave much time to solve the problems of congestion, not only in the air, but also at airports and access to them" Dormoy said.

"Sooner or later, the big hubs will be full. There will be a point where they cannot absorb any more traffic, even by reducing passenger service standards," he added. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
